en:
Welcome to college! 

Your Sim's college career is tracked by semesters, 2 per class year: Freshman, Sophomore, Junior, and Senior. The amount of time left in your Sim's semester is shown in the Semester Timer. Hover your mouse cursor over the current semester in the timer to see how many hours are remaining until your final, which marks the end of your Sim's semester. If your Sim makes it through all four years of college, they will graduate and move back to their home neighborhood.

Sims who have a college degree will have new career tracks available to them, and will be better prepared to perform well in their jobs.

Watch out, if your Sim drops out or gets expelled from college, they can never come back.

en:
This panel contains all the information you need to know about how your Sims are doing in college. It lists your Sim's current major, which you can change by contacting the registrar on the phone by choosing "Call...College" and then choosing "Registrar - Change Major" or "Registrar - Declare Major." You can also change your major by clicking on the computer and choosing "College" and then choosing "Registrar - Change Major" or "Registrar - Declare Major."

Displayed here is the name of your Sim's current class and what time it meets every day. Sims in a good mood will go to class automatically. You can force not-so-happy Sims to go by clicking on the active Sim and choosing "College... Go to Class."

This panel also shows your Sim's GPA, which is the average of all the previously completed semesters' grades, shown on a 4 point scale.

en:
The Class Performance Meter shows how well your Sim is performing in the current semester. The Meter is increased when your Sim does academic activities such as doing their Assignments, going to Class and more. The Meter can only hold so much performance, however, and your Sim is wasting time if they study when the meter is full. Having your Sims build the indicated Skills expands the meter, opening up more room to fill with academic activities. Your Sim gets the best possible grade when they completely expand the meter and fill it up to the top. 

When the Semester Timer reaches its end, your Sim will have to go to their Final Exam. Sims in a good mood will go to their Final by themselves, but you can send any Sim to their Final by clicking on them when they are active and choosing "College...Go to Final Exam." Sending your Sim to their Final Exam in a good mood can give a nice boost to your Sim's Class Performance, assuming there’s room left in the meter. If your Sim misses their Final Exam, however, their Class Performance will drop! Your final exam may not occur during your normal class time, so keep an eye on the semester timer.

If your Sim ends the semester with their Class Performance Meter filled below the white line, your Sim will have to repeat the semester on Academic Probation - if they fail to pass the semester while on Academic Probation, they're kicked out of college forever!

en:
There are three different types of lots you can live on at college: Dorms, Private Residences, and Greek Houses.
 
If your Sims are living in a dorm, you might want to go claim a bedroom for each Sim before the other students show up. Click on the door to the room your Sim wants and select the "Claim Door" interaction.  A Sim can only claim one room. If you get tired of Sims just barging in, just use the "Lock Door" interaction.

Moving into a private residence is as easy as picking up the newspaper or using the computer and choosing "Find Own Place".

If you'd like to move into a Greek House - call up the house you'd like to join on the phone using the "Greek House.../Join" interaction.

en:
In addition to being great places to build skills and meet people, community lots in college offer some exciting moneymaking opportunities. Visit the campus lounge and take over for the Barista making espresso, play music for tips, or hit the campus gym and be a personal trainer!
 
Perhaps the easiest way of keeping some cash in your Sims' pockets is to make sure they get good grades - the school will award grants to students that perform well.

en:
Put your pesky dorm-mates to work! Your Sims now have an "Influence" meter, which is filled up by completing special Influence Wants that have a blue border in the Wants panel. Raise the maximum amount of achievable influence for your Sim by getting them more friends. 
 
To use influence, click on a Sim and choose "Influence To" and then pick a task. Get them to clean up for you, cook you some food, or even weed your garden! 
 
The cost of a particular influence interaction is listed in parentheses after its name. If "Influence To" is grayed out, your Sim doesn't have enough influence yet!

To see this Mini-Tutorial again, go to the Options Mode panel, open the Game Options subpanel, and then click the "Reset Mini-Tutorial" button. Then exit the lot and re-enter any lot that has a household moved in. The Mini-Tutorial will play again.
